Add nicknames to the cloud save, and the handoff

The player picks a nickname (3 to 16 letters, digits, _ or dot), unique
ignoring case and accents, with reserved names and offensive words
refused by the server; the recovery code stays the only way in. The
migration adds gta_nick_check and gta_nick_set and returns the nickname
with the save; it was run twice on a local Postgres 16 with Supabase's
default grants, as anon. The panel becomes 'Apelido e outro aparelho'
and the start card says who is playing. Still off: the migration has
not been applied to the project.

HANDOFF.md has the request, the state, the order of what is pending and
what lives outside git, for the next session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add the cloud copy of the save, and the export for a native PC build

Cloud: no account; each player holds a 160-bit recovery code and the
server keeps only its SHA-256, behind two RPC functions
(supabase/migrations/20261112210000_gta_saves_v1.sql). The game pulls,
merges and pushes with plain fetch, and the start card gets a panel to
show this device's code or take another device's. It is off in
src/data/nuvem.json: the migration has not been applied.

Native build: DLSS only runs in native games, so docs/ALTO-NIVEL.md plans
an Unreal Engine 5 version that reuses this game's data, and
tools/export_engine.py writes it (16-bit Landscape heightmap with its
scale and axes, water mask, missions with points in Unreal centimetres,
the save contract). The heightmap is checked by reading it back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016x9mP2r39qzK6XW7QWLfrF

Save the player's progress, and continue from it

Progress is autosaved in the browser at every ticked mission (with a
'Progresso salvo' pill), every 15 s of play when he has moved, and when
the page is hidden. The save is versioned and checked on every read: a
corrupt one is kept aside and the last good copy used, one written by a
newer build is neither read nor overwritten, and a browser that refuses
storage lets the game go on and says so. The start card offers to
continue the run in progress (mission, counter, followers and his place),
to start over with a second tap, or to replay a finished episode while
keeping its record. mergeSaves() is ready for a cloud copy and never
loses a finished mission.

Load meshes without meshopt, from .glb or .glb.json, and read #flags

The claude.ai page does not serve .glb and passes no query string. The
game now fetches a model's bytes from <name>.glb, or from <name>.glb.json
({ b64 }) when the host serves no GLB, and reads #alta, #baixa and #fps
from the hash. Meshes are quantized instead of meshopt-compressed, so the
loader needs no WebAssembly that a host's CSP could block; the budget
test refuses a mesh that still requires EXT_meshopt_compression.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Open the repository: contributing guide, data license, meshes out of git

Alex asked for the game's code to be open so others can build it with us.
The code stays MIT; the data files keep their sources' licenses
(LICENSE-DATA.md); the Tripo meshes have their own license and are not
in the repository (.gitignore), registered with hashes in ASSETS.md. The
game falls back to the simple shapes without them, and the mesh budget
test skips an absent file. CONTRIBUTING.md has setup, the branch and PR
flow, and the project's rules. ASSETS.md records the split: Codex makes
and rigs the meshes, Claude keeps gameplay and integration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Put the Tripo hero in the game with a provisional rig

The first heroi.glb from Tripo has 1,959,077 triangles, 4K textures, faces
+X and has no skeleton or animations. tools/optimize_model.mjs brings it to
17,991 triangles and 2048 WebP textures (22.3 MB -> 867 KB); src/rig.ts bakes
it to the game frame and skins it to an 11-bone skeleton guessed from the
geometry, so the walk cycle lowers the A-pose arms and moves the legs.
A file with its own skin or animations is refused by that path and falls
back to the simple shapes until the mixer is wired against a real file.

Adds the mesh viewer (tools/viewer, tools/check_model.mjs), a budget test
for every mesh in src/data/modelos.json, ASSETS.md with the received file's
numbers and the Claude/Codex file split. Originals stay out of git in
assets-src/.

Serve heights as JSON, flank followers, one prompt on phones

Heights move from .bin to base64 JSON so any static host serves them; the
test checks the decoder against the builder's SHA-256. Followers walk beside
the player instead of between him and the camera. On a phone the round
button is the only action prompt. The FPS counter uses real time (the game
clock is capped at 50 ms a frame, which made a 1 fps run read 20 fps).

Start the vertical slice: Pescadores de gente at Capernaum

Playable prototype in three.js (WebGPU renderer with WebGL 2 fallback),
Vite and TypeScript: the real relief of the Capernaum shore, the player in
third person with the camera behind him, the three missions of Mark 1:16-20,
the HUD of the reels with literal BLIVRE lines, and visible credits.

tools/build_world.py makes the world data from open sources (AWS Terrain
Tiles, OpenBible.info places, BLIVRE verses) with tile hashes; the tests
check every line against its verse and play the episode through.
